sections.content: You know basic directions from A1 (Unit 16). On the street both tú (casual) and usted (formal/stranger) forms are common. Here are the core directional verbs in both forms:

sections.title: Direction Commands
rows: ¡Gira a la derecha! / ¡Gire a la derecha!
¡Dobla a la izquierda! / ¡Doble a la izquierda!

items.spanish: Siga todo recto hasta la plaza y luego gire a la izquierda.
items.english: Go straight ahead until the square and then turn left.

items.spanish: Cruza el puente y toma la segunda calle a la derecha.
items.english: Cross the bridge and take the second street on the right.

sections.content: Both 'girar' and 'doblar' mean 'to turn' and are understood everywhere.
